thread:
Maria Chen: heads up — spotted a pattern in last night's spot drains where a single region lost ~40% of GPUs and our fallback caused a big latency spike. thinking we need a smoother handoff than the current 'instant top-up' to on-demand.
Ajay Patel: ugh, saw the alert. how big was the request surge during that window?
Maria Chen: not huge — about 1.3x baseline. problem was eviction churn + immediate routing to on-demand which saturated a small on-demand pool. p95 went from 220ms to 1.6s.
Devon Reyes: idea: instead of an instant floor-fill, we ramp on-demand allocation in a "slope" over N seconds and simultaneously move lower-priority work into a burst spot lane that tolerates retries.
Lee Carter: ^ this. a short ramp lets in-flight KV cache warmups and prevents cold-surge amplification. what's a reasonable ramp window? 30s? 2m?
Ajay Patel: 2m seems long for interactive SLOs. could be parameterized by request mix: 30s for latency-critical routes, 120s for batch.
Sarah O'Neill: agree. also add a stochastic jitter to avoid many tenants hitting the ramp at the same instant — e.g., per-tenant ramp offset 0-15s.
Maria Chen: prototype config I sketched:
```json
{"policy":"slope","ramp_seconds":30,"min_on_demand_pct":0.12,"burst_pool_pct":0.25,"per_tenant_jitter_s":10,"eviction_retry_policy":"exponential-backoff, max-tries=3"}
```
Maria Chen: notes: min_on_demand_pct is a soft floor (we try to keep that % of capacity on-demand), slope ramps up to required pct over ramp_seconds. burst_pool_pct seeds a short-lived spot pool for retriable jobs.
Devon Reyes: how do we define "retriable"? embeddings & long-running generation jobs are different. we should tag requests with retryable=true only when idempotent or user-tolerant.
Ajay Patel: add adaptive throttling: if on-demand queue > X and p95 latency > Y, start shedding lower-tier traffic to burst pool earlier. tie to a simple linear policy.
Lee Carter: can we simulate this with last month's trace? would help quantify cost impact vs SLO.
Sarah O'Neill: yes — I'll run a replay with two knobs: ramp_seconds & min_on_demand_pct. output: p95, interrupted_count, on_demand_cost_delta.
infra-bot: scheduled job queued: trace-replay/1748504321-run-1 (owner: sarah.o) — ETA ~ 2h
Maria Chen: thanks. action items: Sarah runs replay + posts results, Ajay updates routing code to accept ramp config and jitter, Devon to add request-level retryable tagging docs. I'll draft an RFC for the slope fallback model after we have replay metrics.
Ajay Patel: I'll also add a cheap safety: if on-demand backfills are >60% of burst cost delta, abort slope and fallback to instant fill (safety kill).
Sarah O'Neill: got it, starting the replay now. will post a short summary in ~2h. :thumbsup:
Devon Reyes: one more thing — watch KV cache hit rate during ramp; if cache misses spike we might need a warm-warmup phase for critical models.
Maria Chen: good call. include cache_hit_rate in the replay outputs.
Lee Carter: 👍 let's keep the initial ramp conservative. no one wants a 3x bill overnight.
Maria Chen: agreed — thanks all, will follow up with RFC and estimated rollout stages once we have numbers.
